cues.en: Hi.
cues.zh: 嗨。

cues.en: Today we're gonna talk about Pascal's wager and Pascal's mugging. This is necessarily going to touch on religious topics pretty heavily actually and I'm just gonna say at the beginning of the video that personally I don't believe that any god or gods have ever existed and I'm not gonna pretend otherwise in this video. So be forewarned if that's likely to bother you. So as you may know, Pascal was a seventeenth century philosopher who was interested in amongst other things, the question of the existence of the Christian God.
cues.zh: 今天我们要聊帕斯卡的赌注和帕斯卡的敲诈。这必然会相当多地涉及宗教话题。我先在视频开头说明：我个人不相信任何神曾经存在过，这个视频里我也不会假装不是这样。所以如果你可能会介意，请提前有心理准备。你可能知道，帕斯卡是17世纪哲学家，他感兴趣的问题之一就是基督教上帝是否存在。

cues.en: Various philosophers at the time were arguing that God didn't exist and there was a lot of discussion going on about the various kinds of evidence for and against God in the world. But there's this thing that's quite common when people think about religious questions
cues.zh: 当时很多哲学家在争论上帝不存在，大家也大量讨论世界上支持和反对上帝存在的各种证据。但人们思考宗教问题时，有一种很常见的现象

cues.en: where it feels sort of unsatisfying
cues.zh: 就是会觉得有点不满足

cues.en: to talk about worldly evidence as if you were considering some everyday question.
cues.zh: 用世俗证据来讨论，仿佛是在考虑某个日常问题。

cues.en: There's a feeling that these supernatural concepts are very grand and mysterious.
cues.zh: 人们会觉得，这些超自然概念非常宏大而神秘。

cues.en: They're special and so just straightforwardly considering the evidence for and against God is not the right way to do things. This is of course encouraged by religious thinking.
cues.zh: 它们很特殊，所以直接去权衡支持和反对上帝的证据并不是正确做法。宗教思维当然会助长这种想法。

cues.en: The idea that some hypotheses aren't subject to the usual rules of evidence and logic is pretty appealing if you want to advocate for an idea that doesn't fare very well by those standards. I suspect Pascal may have felt something like that because his position was that reason has nothing to say about the question of whether or not God exists. It's sort of an unknowable thing. And instead,
cues.zh: 有些假说不受通常的证据和逻辑规则约束——如果你想鼓吹一个按这些标准并不怎么站得住脚的观点，这种想法就很有吸引力。我怀疑帕斯卡可能有类似感受，因为他的立场是：理性对上帝是否存在这个问题无话可说。这算是某种不可知的东西。而相反，

cues.en: he proposed that we should make a wager. We should think about it like this. There are two possibilities.
cues.zh: 他提出我们应该打个赌。我们可以这样想。存在两种可能。

cues.en: Either the Christian God exists or he doesn't. And reason gives us no way to choose between those. We have two options available to us. Either we can live according to God's laws and act as though we believe or we can not do that. So we have a sort of payoff matrix here with four sections.
cues.zh: 基督教上帝要么存在，要么不存在。而理性无法让我们在两者之间做出选择。我们有两种选择：要么按照上帝的律法生活，表现得好像我们信他；要么不这么做。所以这就形成了一个有四个部分的收益矩阵。

cues.en: If God exists and we believe in him, then we get infinite reward in heaven. If God exists and we don't believe in him, we get infinite punishment in hell. If God doesn't exist and we believe in him, then we pay some costs. You know, there are some rules we have to follow and so on. And if he doesn't exist and we don't believe in him, then maybe we get a few perks from not believing, like having a lion on Sundays and being right. Pascal's point is that this payoff matrix is completely dominated by the case in which God exists
cues.zh: 如果上帝存在而我们信他，我们就能上天堂，获得无限的奖励。如果上帝存在而我们不信他，我们就会下地狱，受到无限的惩罚。如果上帝不存在而我们信他，我们就要付出一些代价，比如得遵守一些规则等等。如果他不存在而我们也不信他，那我们或许还能因为不信而得到点好处，比如周日能睡个懒觉，而且自己还是对的。帕斯卡的观点是：这个收益矩阵完全由“上帝存在”那种情况所主导。

cues.en: because we're talking about infinite rewards and infinite punishments
cues.zh: 因为我们说的是无限的奖赏和无限的惩罚

cues.en: as opposed to the other case with these very finite costs and benefits. So regardless of the evidence, Pascal argues we should believe in God or at least act like it because it's just the sensible bet to make. This is really kind of a nice argument from Pascal's perspective because it doesn't need evidence at all.
cues.zh: 而不是另一种情况，成本和收益都非常有限。所以不管证据如何，Pascal 认为我们都应该信仰上帝，或者至少表现得像信一样，因为这就是一个明智的赌注。从 Pascal 的角度看，这其实是个挺妙的论证，因为它根本不需要证据。

cues.en: No finite earthly evidence can outweigh infinite supernatural payoffs. It feels like the kind of clean abstract reasoning that you're supposed to do when thinking about the supernatural. All of this hard work looking at history and psychology and science and trying to figure out where the ideas of religion come from and whether our world seems like the kind of world with a God in it. It's long winded, confusing,
cues.zh: 任何有限的世俗证据都无法压过无限的超自然回报。这感觉就像思考超自然事物时该做的那种清晰纯粹的抽象推理。所有这些辛苦工作——考察历史、心理学和科学，试图弄清楚宗教观念从何而来，以及我们的世界是否像是那种有上帝存在的世界。它冗长又令人困惑，

cues.en: it's it's just messy. But here we just have a clean argument that says we should believe in God or at least act like it and that seems very neat. No evidence required. So consider now, Pascal is walking down the street and he stopped by a shady looking man who says, give me your wallet.
cues.zh: it's it's just messy. 但这里我们有一个很干净的论证：我们应该相信上帝，至少表现得像相信一样，而这看起来非常整洁。不需要证据。那么现在设想，Pascal走在街上，被一个看起来很可疑的人拦住，对方说：把钱包给我。

cues.en: I would prefer not to.
cues.zh: 我更不想给。

cues.en: Do you even have a weapon? No. UK laws are very strict about that but I don't need one because I'm God. You're God. Yep. I'm God and Christianity got a lot of things wrong about me, my forgiving nature, my infinite mercy and so on. But the infinite torture thing is legit
cues.zh: 你带武器了吗？没有。英国法律对这种事非常严格，但我不需要武器，因为我是上帝。你是上帝。对。我是上帝，基督教对我有很多地方都搞错了：我的宽容本性、我的无限慈悲等等。但无限折磨那件事是真的，

cues.en: and if you don't give me your wallet right now, I will torture you for eternity in the afterlife. Now if you're Pascal, you're in kind of a difficult situation
cues.zh: 如果你现在不把钱包给我，我就会在来世永远折磨你。现在如果你是Pascal，你就有点进退两难了。

cues.en: because the fact that it seems very unlikely that this mugger actually is God is not meant to be part of your calculation. Your argument is one of pure logic. It works independently of any evidence.
cues.zh: 因为这个劫匪实际上极不可能是上帝，而这一点本来就不该算进你的计算里。你的论证是纯逻辑的。它不依赖任何证据也能成立。

cues.en: You didn't need to look for evidence of the Christian God and you don't need to look for evidence that this mugger is God either. So you kind of have to give him your wallet.
cues.zh: 你不需要去寻找基督教上帝存在的证据，也不需要去寻找这个劫匪就是上帝的证据。所以你还真有点不得不把钱包交给他。

cues.en: And now you're really in trouble because of course when this gets out there's gonna be a line around the block of Erzat's deities asking for handouts.
cues.zh: 现在你可真麻烦了，因为这事一旦传出去，Erzat 的众神肯定会排着队绕街区一圈来讨施舍。

cues.en: How are you gonna deal with this endless stream of fizzy gods? Well, one thing you can do is you can play the muggers off against one another. You can bring in two of them and say, listen, you say that you're gonna torture me forever if I don't give you my wallet. And you say the same thing. I only have one wallet, so it looks like whatever I do, I'm gonna be tortured forever by somebody. And if I'm going to be infinitely tortured anyway, well, two times infinity is still just infinity, so I may as well hang on to the wallet.
cues.zh: 你打算怎么应付这没完没了、不断冒泡的神明？有个办法：让这些劫匪互相牵制。你可以把其中两个叫来，说：听着，你说如果我不把钱包给你，你就会永远折磨我。你也这么说。可我只有一个钱包，所以不管我怎么做，看起来总会有个人永远折磨我。既然反正都要被无限折磨，那两倍无限还是无限，所以我还不如留着钱包。

cues.en: Now get the hell out of my house. Alright. Next two. No doubt these self proclaimed deities may try to argue that they have some reason why they are in fact a real deity and this other mugger is just a random guy who's pretending.
cues.zh: 现在滚出我家。好，接下来两个。毫无疑问，这些自称神明的人可能会辩称，他们有某种理由说明自己确实是真神，而另一个劫匪只是个随便冒充的家伙。

cues.en: But that's all worldly evidence which you've decided isn't required for your argument. And the muggers don't really want you to become interested in evidence because, well, the evidence points very strongly towards none of them being real gods. So this is a better position to be in. You're still spending a lot of your time arguing with charlatans,
cues.zh: 但那都是世俗证据，而你已经认定你的论证不需要这些。劫匪其实并不希望你开始关心证据，因为证据非常强烈地表明，他们中没有一个是真神。所以这还算是个更好的处境。你仍然花大量时间跟江湖骗子争论，

cues.en: at but least you still have your wallet. And you don't actually have to pair them up against each other. Right? You can just make up a deity.
cues.zh: 但至少你的钱包还在。而且你其实不必让他们互相对质，对吧？你完全可以自己编一个神出来。

cues.en: When someone comes in pretending to be a god, you can say, oh, well, there's this other god who demands exactly the opposite thing from you. A goddess actually and she's very powerful
cues.zh: 当有人跑来假装自己是神，你可以说，哦，好吧，还有另一位神，她对你要求的正好相反。其实是位女神，而且她非常强大

cues.en: but she goes to a different school. You wouldn't know her. Really? Yeah. She lives in Canada.
cues.zh: 但她上的是另一所学校。你不会认识她。真的？对。她住在加拿大。

cues.en: She's omnipresent
cues.zh: 她无处不在

cues.en: obviously
cues.zh: 显然

cues.en: but she lives in Canada. Anyway, she says that I'm not to give you the wallet and if I do then she'll torture me forever in the afterlife.
cues.zh: 但她住在加拿大。总之，她说我不能把钱包给你，如果我给了，她会在来世永远折磨我。

cues.en: Dang. Yeah.
cues.zh: 靠。是啊。

cues.en: So you can solve a lot of these problems by inventing gods arbitrarily and of course this applies just as well to the original version of Pascal's wager because although it's implied that this payoff matrix has enumerated all of the possibilities and in a sense it has, the Christian God either exists or he doesn't. Nonetheless, those may not be the only things that affect the payoffs. For any given God, you can take the God down, flip it, and reverse it, and say, what about anti God who wants me to do the exact opposite and promises the exact opposite consequence? Now you can see that they cancel out. Somebody who's arguing for the existence of the first god might say, k, but this anti god is just made up, which I mean,
cues.zh: 所以，你可以通过随便发明神来解决很多这类问题，当然这同样适用于帕斯卡赌注的原版，因为虽然它暗示这个收益矩阵已经枚举了所有可能性，某种意义上确实如此——基督教上帝要么存在，要么不存在。尽管如此，影响收益的可能并不只有这些。对任何一个给定的神，你都可以把神拿下来、翻转、再倒过来，然后说：那反神呢？他想要我做完全相反的事，并承诺完全相反的后果。现在你能看到，它们相互抵消了。为第一个神的存在辩护的人可能会说：行，但这个反神只是编出来的，我的意思是，

cues.en: yeah, it is. It's true that the situation isn't really symmetrical.
cues.zh: 是的，确实如此。情况确实并不真正对称。

cues.en: Someone might think God is more likely than anti God because of evidence from the Bible and there's no such thing as the anti Bible and so on. The point is though, we're back to talking about the evidence. That's really the problem I have with Pascal's wager. The way it uses infinite costs and infinite benefits to completely override our necessarily finite evidence.
cues.zh: 有人可能会觉得，根据圣经中的证据，上帝比反上帝更可能存在，而且不存在什么反圣经之类的东西。但关键在于，我们又回到了证据这个问题上。这正是我对帕斯卡赌注的真正问题所在。它用无限代价和无限收益，完全压过了我们必然有限的证据。

cues.en: But what if the cost and benefits aren't infinite just very very large?
cues.zh: 但如果成本和收益并非无限，而只是非常非常大呢？

cues.en: That ends up being a much more interesting question. On one end of the scale, we can easily name numbers so large that no amount of evidence anyone could ever actually gather in their lifetime could have an impact on the conclusion. We can specify costs and benefits that are technically finite but that still feel very much like a Pascal's wager. On the other end of the scale, if you come across a bet that pays out 10,000 to one on an event with a probability of one in a 100, that's a very good bet to take.
cues.zh: 这就成了一个有趣得多的问题。在尺度的一端，我们可以轻易举出大到任何人一生中实际能收集到的证据都不足以影响结论的数字。我们可以指定技术上有限、但感觉仍很像帕斯卡赌注的成本和收益。在尺度的另一端，如果你遇到一个以 10,000 比 1 赔付、而事件概率为百分之一的赌局，那非常值得下注。

cues.en: Someone could complain that it's a Pascal's wager to bet on an unlikely outcome just because the payoff is so high, but if you take enough bets like that, you're sure to become very rich. In the same way, if there's a button which has a one in a million chance of starting a global thermonuclear war, it's still worth expending significant resources to stop that button being pressed. One in a million isn't much, but the cost of a nuclear war is really high. I don't think that's a Pascal's wager either. The difference seems to come in somewhere in the gap between very small probabilities of very large costs and benefits and really extremely small probabilities
cues.zh: 有人可能会抱怨：仅因为回报极高，就去赌一个不太可能发生的结果，这是一种帕斯卡赌注；但如果你下足够多这样的赌注，你肯定会变得非常富有。同样，如果有一个按钮，有百万分之一的概率引发全球热核战争，那仍然值得投入大量资源去阻止它被按下。百万分之一并不算高，但核战争的代价实在太高了。我也不认为那算帕斯卡赌注。区别似乎就在“很大成本与收益对应很小概率”和“极小概率”之间的某个地方

cues.en: of near infinite costs and benefits. So why are we talking about this? What does this have to do with AI safety? Well, suppose somebody stops you in the street and says, hey, if we ever create powerful artificial general intelligence,
cues.zh: 对应近乎无限的成本与收益。那为什么我们要谈这个？这和 AI 安全有什么关系？好吧，假设有人在街上拦住你说：嘿，如果我们有一天创造出强大的通用人工智能，

cues.en: then that will have a tremendous impact. In fact, the future of the whole of humanity hinges on it. If we get it right, we could have human flourishing for the rest of time. If we get it wrong, we could have human extinction or worse. Regardless of how likely superhuman AGI is, the potential impact is so high that it makes AI safety research tremendously important.
cues.zh: 那将产生巨大影响。事实上，全人类的未来都系于此。如果我们做对了，人类就能永远繁荣。如果我们做错了，就可能人类灭绝，甚至更糟。无论超级人类 AGI 的可能性有多大，潜在影响都如此之高，因此 AI 安全研究极其重要。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: give me your wallet. It's been claimed by some that this is more or less what AI safety as a field is doing. This is kind of an interesting point. As AI safety advocates, are we victims of Pascal's mugging or are we in fact Pascal's muggers ourselves?
cues.zh: 把你的钱包给我。有人声称，这差不多就是 AI 安全这个领域正在做的事。这是个挺有意思的观点。作为 AI 安全倡导者，我们是帕斯卡抢劫的受害者，还是我们自己其实才是帕斯卡式的劫匪？

cues.en: Well, if people were saying these AI risks may be extremely unlikely but the consequences of getting AI wrong are so huge that it's worth spending a lot of resources on regardless of the probabilities so we don't even need to consider the evidence. Well, I would consider that to be a Pascal's wager style bad argument. But what I actually hear is not that.
cues.zh: 如果人们说的是，这些 AI 风险可能极不可能发生，但把 AI 搞错的后果如此巨大，以至于不管概率多低都值得投入大量资源，所以我们甚至不需要考虑证据。那我会认为这是一种帕斯卡赌注式的糟糕论证。但我实际听到的并不是这个。

cues.en: What I hear is more like, look, we're not completely sure about this. It's quite possible that we're wrong. But considering the enormity of what's at stake, it's definitely worth allocating more resources to AI safety than we currently are. That sounds pretty similar, but that's mostly because natural language is extremely vague when talking about uncertainty.
cues.zh: 我听到的更像是：你看，我们对此并不完全确定。我们很可能错了。但考虑到利害关系如此巨大，我们绝对值得在 AI 安全上投入比现在更多的资源。这听起来很相似，但这主要是因为自然语言在谈论不确定性时极其模糊。

cues.en: There's an enormous difference in the probabilities being talked about. In the same way, if when you talk to AI safety researchers, they said things like, well, I think the chance of any of this ever being relevant are really extremely tiny. It seems more or less impossible to me, but I've decided to work on it anyway because the potential costs and benefits are so unimaginably vast. Then yeah, I'd be a little concerned that they might be victims of Pascal's mugging. But when you ask AI safety researchers, they don't think that the probability of their work ever becoming relevant is very tiny.
cues.zh: 这里谈到的概率有天壤之别。同样地，如果你去问 AI 安全研究人员，他们会说：“嗯，我觉得这一切有朝一日会变得相关的概率真的极其微小。”这在我看来几乎不可能，但我还是决定做下去，因为潜在的成本和收益大到难以想象。那我确实会有点担心，他们可能是帕斯卡式打劫的受害者。但当你去问 AI 安全研究人员时，他们并不认为自己的工作有朝一日会变得相关的概率非常小。

cues.en: They don't necessarily think it's huge either, maybe not even more than 50%.
cues.zh: 他们也不一定认为它很大，也许甚至不超过50%。

cues.en: But it's not so small that you have to rely on the unimaginable vastness of the consequences in order to make the argument. To borrow a metaphor from Stuart Russell,
cues.zh: 但它也没有小到你必须依靠后果那难以想象的巨大规模来论证。借用 Stuart Russell 的一个比喻，

cues.en: suppose you're part of a team working on building a bridge and you believe you found a flaw in the design that could cause the structure to fail catastrophically.
cues.zh: 假设你是一个建桥团队的一员，你相信自己发现了设计中的一个缺陷，可能导致结构灾难性失效。

cues.en: Maybe the disaster would only happen if there's a very rare combination of weather conditions, and there's only a one in a 100 chance that those conditions will ever happen during the course of the bridge's expected lifespan. And further suppose that you're not completely sure of your calculations because this kind of thing is complicated. Maybe you only give yourself a 40% chance of being right about this. So you go to the civil engineer in charge of the project and you say, I think there's a serious risk with this bridge design. Do you think the bridge is gonna collapse? Probably not. No. But I'm about 40% sure that there's a design flaw which would give this bridge a one in 100 chance of catastrophic failure. So you're telling me that in the event of a scenario which is very unlikely to happen, the bridge might collapse and you yourself admit that you're more likely to be wrong than right about this. Stop wasting my time. But if the bridge collapses it could kill a lot of people. I think this is a Pascal's mugging. Don't try to get me to ignore the low probabilities just by threatening very large consequences.
cues.zh: 也许灾难只有在极其罕见的气象条件组合下才会发生，而这些条件在桥梁预期寿命内出现的概率只有百分之一。再假设你对自己的计算并不完全有把握，因为这类事情很复杂。也许你只给自己 40% 的把握认为这是对的。于是你去找负责项目的土木工程师，说：我认为这个桥梁设计存在严重风险。你觉得桥会塌吗？大概不会。不会。但我有大约 40% 的把握认为存在设计缺陷，会让这座桥有百分之一的灾难性失效概率。所以你是说，在一个极不可能发生的情况下，桥可能会塌，而你自己也承认，你更可能是错的而不是对的。别浪费我时间了。但如果桥塌了，可能会死很多人。我觉得这是帕斯卡式敲诈。别想只靠威胁说后果极其严重，就让我忽略那些低概率。

cues.en: Obviously, isn't what would happen. No civil engineer is going to accept a one in two hundred and fifty chance of catastrophic failure for a major piece of infrastructure because civil engineers have a healthy organizational culture around safety. What it comes down to again is the difference between different levels of improbability.
cues.zh: 显然，事情不会这样发生。没有土木工程师会接受重大基础设施有 1/250 的灾难性故障概率，因为土木工程师围绕安全有着健康的组织文化。归根结底，还是不同级别的不可能性之间的差别。

cues.en: The chance of an AGI catastrophe may not be very big but it's much much larger than the chance that a mugger is actually a god. And what about our anti god tactic?
cues.zh: AGI 灾难的概率可能并不很大，但远远大于一个劫匪其实是神的概率。那我们那条“反神”策略呢？

cues.en: Finding the opposite risk, does that still work? Like what if we consider the possibility that there's another opposite design flaw in the bridge which might cause it to collapse unless we don't spend extra time evaluating the safety of the design? What? Just look at the schematic, would you? And what if working on AI safety actually ends up making the risks worse somehow?
cues.zh: 找出相反的风险，这还成立吗？比如，要是我们考虑另一种相反设计缺陷的可能性——这座桥可能因此倒塌，除非我们不额外花时间评估设计的安全性？什么？你就看一眼示意图，行吗？还有，如果研究 AI 安全最后反而以某种方式让风险更糟呢？

cues.en: I think this actually is worth considering. Unintended consequences are a real problem after all. Speaking generally, there's a clear argument that the future is very important and that we're probably able to have a very big impact on it, but it's hard to know for sure whether that impact will be positive or negative for any given course of action. Prediction is very difficult as they say, especially about the future. And the further into the future we look, the more difficult it gets. Like imagine if you lived in the year 1900
cues.zh: 我觉得这确实值得考虑。毕竟意外后果是个真实的问题。总的来说，有明确论点认为未来非常重要，而且我们很可能能对它产生巨大影响，但对于任何给定行动方案，很难确定这种影响是正面还是负面。俗话说，预测很难，尤其是预测未来。而且我们看得越远，就越难。比如想象你生活在 1900 年

cues.en: and you had some insight that made you realize that nuclear weapons were possible and nuclear war was a risk. You'd hope that you could use that understanding to reduce the risk, but it would certainly be possible to make things worse by accident. In the case of AI safety though, I don't see that being anywhere near as much of a concern.
cues.zh: 你曾有过某种洞见，让你意识到核武器是可能造出来的，核战争是一种风险。你会希望用这种理解来降低风险，但确实也有可能意外地把事情弄得更糟。不过在 AI 安全这件事上，我不认为这会是同等程度的担忧。

cues.en: We're heading towards AI regardless and it seems very unlikely that thinking about safety would be more dangerous than not thinking about safety. It's definitely possible to make things worse while trying to make them better, but you can't avoid that by never trying to make things better. I guess my point is there's just no getting around the messy, confusing, complicated work of looking at and thinking about the evidence.
cues.zh: 无论如何，我们都在走向 AI，而思考安全问题会比不思考安全问题更危险，这似乎极不可能。试图把事情变好时，确实可能把事情弄糟，但你不能靠从不尝试把事情变好来避免这一点。我想说的是，审视并思考证据这件混乱、令人困惑又复杂的工作，根本绕不开。

cues.en: Any argument that doesn't rely on the evidence will work equally well whatever the truth is. So at the end of the day, that kind of thing isn't going to give you an answer. You have to just stare at the bridge design and really think. You have to actually do the engineering. And that's something I'm trying to get across with this channel. You won't find me saying never mind the evidence, AI safety is important because it could have huge consequences.
cues.zh: 不依赖证据的论证，无论事实如何都同样成立。所以说到底，这类说法不会给你答案。你得盯着桥梁设计，认真思考。你得真正去做工程。这正是我想通过这个频道传达的。你不会听到我说：别管证据，AI 安全很重要，因为它可能带来巨大后果。

cues.en: What I do on this channel is I try to show you some of the evidence and some of the arguments and let you think about the situation and draw your own conclusions. It can be tricky and involved. It requires some thought,
cues.zh: 这个频道里，我会尽量给你展示一些证据和论点，让你自己思考整个情况并得出自己的结论。这可能很棘手也很复杂，需要动点脑筋，

cues.en: but it has the advantage of being the only thing that has any chance of actually getting the right answer.
